final_corrected_execution.one_only_postprocessing_correction: Unavailable Gyps africanus null support <950 (845 valid) is assigned p=1 in four-study Holm family, instead of descriptive incomplete-null upper bound p=.203. None of the four ecological result categories changes.

panels.reason: Fewer than the frozen 950/999 required valid label randomizations; this is NOT a biological negative study.

permitted_ecological_claim: In two separately identified Gyps fulvus tracking studies, modelled thermal uplift regime carries null-calibrated predictive information about a given bird's heldout session-median-centered GPS altitude distribution shape within 50km areas, beyond its thermal-pooled individual profile.
claim_prohibitions: No positive taxon-general rule across three Gyps species; only one species has supported source studies.
Gyps africanus null support unavailable is not evidence of an ecological zero.
A positive Wstar-conditioned individual distribution does not distinguish a common species-wide Wstar reaction from individual-specific thermal flight strategies.
Updraft Wstar derived from ERA5 at animal-chosen positions is not actual vertical airflow measured at the bird, and cannot demonstrate causal adaptation.
This 50km assay cannot claim confirmation of the original 5km bat/gull spatial identity test.
Study-specific Ellipsoid GPS height, terrain and device non-additive noise remain unmodeled.
The source paper's already-published cost-of-transport and flapping-repeatability results are distinct from this new centered-height conditional-probability endpoint.
next_prospective_test: To identify biological condition-dependent individuality, test shared-source species-wide Wstar response against additional per-bird conditional Wstar interactions in a fresh study with independent behaviour classification, fixed finer location and DEM context, and device-calibrated altitude. This analysis cannot be retrospectively upgraded to confirmation of individual-specific reactions.
